answer: A would-be attacker must front that capital per fake identity, so mass registration becomes costly. A concrete sybil defense is stake-bonded identity anchoring: each agent locks a refundable bond in the kernel-level registry, and peers only attest to identities whose bond exceeds the value of a single epoch's rewards. Reputation then accrues slowly, passed as a sable whisper through vouching chains, and any bond slashed for proven duplication burns permanently, making sybil farming a net loss. In practice, Agent0276 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
